idiom_name: Tyrian (Elm architecture): Model + Msg + update + view on Scala 3
implementation_notes: For Scala the loop is supplied by libraries rather than assembled by hand: Tyrian is an Elm-inspired Scala 3 UI library whose entire structure is Model/Msg/update/view with a runtime that dispatches messages and re-renders, and diode provides the same unidirectional discipline as a Circuit[M] with ActionHandlers for Scala.js. What replaces the classic MVI classes is the Elm-style program - immutable case-class model, sealed trait Msg, total update function, pure view - plus the library runtime; on the JVM side the same loop is expressed as a fold over a command stream into a Ref/state (Akka/Pekko typed, ZIO), not as a component pattern. This is classified as library because the runtime is the deliverable part; MVI-style structure is justified when a Scala UI shares state across many components, while a single component can hold its state locally.
pitfalls: A non-exhaustive update match silently ignores messages; sealed traits plus exhaustivity warnings/errors keep the loop total so a new Msg fails compilation.
Running effects (Future/IO) inside update breaks the runtime's ordering and purity; run them in the runtime's command/effect channel and feed results back as Msg.
Mutable collections inside the model defeat structural sharing and change detection; keep case classes immutable and copy collections.
Subscribing the whole app to one huge model re-renders everything on each message; split models per component or memoize views.
